title: Locally separated targets identify closure-equivalent geometric points
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $\mathcal U$ an algebraic stack over $k$ as defined in [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], $Z/k$ an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space] whose diagonal is an immersion (locally a closed immersion into an open subspace), and $h:\mathcal U\to Z$ a $k$-morphism. Let $\Omega/k$ be an algebraically closed extension and $x_1,x_2\in\mathcal U(\Omega)$. If the closures of their underlying points in $|\mathcal U_\Omega|$ intersect, then $h(x_1)=h(x_2)$ in $Z(\Omega)$. The underlying topology of a stack is the quotient topology from a smooth atlas. No moduli-space morphism is assumed, and neither $\mathcal U$ nor $Z$ is required to be of finite type. Points, the atlas topology and induced continuous maps have the conventions of [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets]; base changes are fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Proposition 7.1.1, proof, printed p.36: surjectivity of the diagonal pullback W from condition (a), expanded as its closure-equivalence input. Rational points of a locally separated space over an algebraically closed field have closed images; continuity gives the assertion. This is the geometric-points sublemma, not the universality conclusion. Read arXiv:1005.2398v3 online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Put $H=h_\Omega:\mathcal U_\Omega\to Z_\Omega$ and $a_i=H(x_i):\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Z_\Omega$. Apply [lem-sfb-locally-separated-rational-point-closed-immersion] with $K=\Omega$ to the given locally separated $k$-space $Z$. Each $a_i$ is a closed immersion and its singleton image $\{z_i\}$ in $|Z_\Omega|$ is closed. This applies without finite type or quasi-separatedness.

Work throughout with algebraic stacks over $\Omega$. Write $u_i=|x_i|$ and choose $w\in\overline{\{u_1\}}\cap\overline{\{u_2\}}$ using the hypothesis. The current continuity clause of [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets], applied with its ground field $k=\Omega$ and morphism $H$, makes $|H|$ continuous. For each $i$, the inverse image $|H|^{-1}\{z_i\}$ is therefore closed and contains $u_i$, so it contains $\overline{\{u_i\}}$. Evaluating at $w$ gives $z_1=|H|(w)=z_2$. Only continuity and the definition of closure are used here; no transitivity of closure-intersection is needed.

proof.text: Form the 2-fibre product $P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\times_{Z_\Omega}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ using $a_1,a_2$, all over $\Omega$. Each spectrum has its unique point, and step 2 says these points have the same image in $|Z_\Omega|$. Thus they give an element of $|\operatorname{Spec}\Omega|\times_{|Z_\Omega|}|\operatorname{Spec}\Omega|$. The current point-surjectivity clause of [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets] gives a preimage in $|P|$, so $P$ is nonempty. By the scheme-pullback clause of [lem-sfb-locally-separated-rational-point-closed-immersion], $P$ is a scheme and its second projection is a closed immersion. By [def-weil-closed-immersion] and [def-weil-affine-spectrum], this is $\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Nonemptiness makes $I$ proper, so $I=0$ by [def-weil-field]. The second projection is therefore an isomorphism; let $s$ be its inverse. Both $p_i s$ are $\Omega$-morphisms from $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ to itself, hence identities. The fibre-product equality $a_1p_1=a_2p_2$ then gives $a_1=a_2$, which is $h(x_1)=h(x_2)$ in $Z(\Omega)$. This uses surjectivity, without identifying the two point sets bijectively.
